title: The JTAG test access port
summary: The **test access port** (TAP) of IEEE 1149.1 is the door into the chip: four or five pins, a 16-state controller driven by one pin (TMS), an instruction register and a set of data registers. Everything else in this training builds on it.
objectives: Name the TAP signals and their roles.
Describe the parts of the TAP: controller, instruction register, data registers.
Follow the TAP state machine and reset it from any state.
Name the control signals the TAP sends to the registers.

blocks.caption: TAP signals of IEEE 1149.1

blocks.title: Timing rule
blocks.md: TMS and TDI are sampled on the **rising** edge of TCK; TDO changes on the **falling** edge. That gives half a clock period for the signal to travel from one chip to the next in a chain.

blocks.caption: TAP controller, instruction register and data registers

blocks.md:
- The **TAP controller** is a 16-state machine clocked by TCK and steered by TMS. It produces the control signals *capture*, *shift* and *update* for the registers.
- The **instruction register (IR)** holds the current instruction. The instruction decides **which data register** sits between TDI and TDO and what the chip does (normal operation, drive pins, run a test …).
- The **data registers (DR)**: BYPASS, IDCODE, the boundary-scan register, and any number of user-defined **test data registers (TDRs)** — for example the registers of the MBIST controllers.

Only **one** register is between TDI and TDO at a time: the IR during an IR scan, the selected DR during a DR scan.

steps.title: Reset and idle
steps.md: **Test-Logic-Reset**: test logic off, the chip works normally. With TMS = 0 the controller moves to **Run-Test/Idle**, where it can wait — and where instruments such as BIST can run.

steps.title: Select and capture
steps.md: TMS = 1 goes to **Select-DR-Scan**, TMS = 0 to **Capture-DR**: the selected data register loads (captures) a value in parallel — for example a status bit or the pin values.

steps.title: Shift
steps.md: In **Shift-DR** each TCK moves the register one bit from TDI towards TDO. The controller stays here as long as TMS = 0.

steps.title: Exit and pause
steps.md: TMS = 1 leaves the shift. **Pause-DR** lets the tester stop shifting for a while — for example to reload its buffer — and **Exit2-DR** returns to shifting.

steps.title: Update
steps.md: **Update-DR** copies the shifted value to the register's parallel outputs in one step. Then TMS = 0 returns to Run-Test/Idle, TMS = 1 starts the next scan.

steps.title: The same for instructions
steps.md: The right column is identical, but works on the **instruction register**. From Select-DR-Scan, TMS = 1 leads to **Select-IR-Scan**; another 1 returns to Test-Logic-Reset.

blocks.title: Five ones reset everything
blocks.md: From **any** state, five TCK clocks with TMS = 1 bring the controller to Test-Logic-Reset. A tester therefore always knows how to get the TAP into a known state, even without TRST*.

blocks.prompt: Practice: what does the register do in each state?

blocks.md: Every test register — IR, BYPASS, boundary scan or an instrument's TDR — is built from the same kind of bit. Click its parts:

blocks.hint: Click the parts of the register bit.
blocks.caption: One bit of a test data register

spots.title: Capture / shift mux
spots.md: Controlled by **ShiftDR**. In Capture-DR it passes the instrument's **status** into the flip-flop; in Shift-DR it passes the bit from the **previous** stage (or TDI).

spots.title: Shift flip-flop
spots.md: Clocked by **ClockDR** (TCK, gated in Capture-DR and Shift-DR). All shift flip-flops together form the shift register between TDI and TDO.

spots.title: Scan path
spots.md: The flip-flop's output goes to the **next bit** — the last bit drives TDO.

spots.title: Update latch
spots.md: Loaded only in **Update-DR** (UpdateDR). It holds the value the instrument uses, so the instrument never sees the bits moving during shift.

spots.title: To the instrument
spots.md: The update latch drives the instrument's **configuration** inputs — for example *start* or the algorithm number of an MBIST controller.

spots.title: From the instrument
spots.md: The instrument's **status** (done, pass, a sensor value) enters through the capture mux in Capture-DR.

steps.title: Before
steps.md: A 3-bit register. The **update latches** hold the configuration 010 that the instrument is using; the instrument reports a status 101.

steps.title: Capture
steps.md: In **Capture-DR** the shift flip-flops load the status 101 in parallel (green arrows).

steps.title: Shift
steps.md: In **Shift-DR** every TCK moves the bits one place: a new bit enters from TDI, a status bit leaves at TDO. The update latches — and so the instrument — do **not** change.

steps.title: Shift complete
steps.md: After 3 clocks the new value 110 is in the shift flip-flops, and the tester has received the status 1 0 1 at TDO.

steps.title: Update
steps.md: In **Update-DR** the latches copy 110 in one step. The instrument switches directly from 010 to 110 — no intermediate values.

items.title: Why capture?
items.md: Capture loads a **new** value into the shift register before it is shifted out — the result of a test, a sensor reading, the values on the pins. Shifting then brings that value to TDO.

items.title: Why a separate update stage?
items.md: While bits travel through the shift register, its outputs change every clock. If an instrument were connected directly, it would see garbage. So most registers have a second, **update** (shadow) stage that changes only in Update-DR — the instrument sees only complete, final values.

items.title: Read and write in one scan
items.md: Capture → shift → update reads the old (captured) value at TDO and writes the new one from TDI in the same scan. Testers use this all the time: write the next configuration and read the last status together.

blocks.md: The TAP controller turns its states into a few **control signals** that go to every test register. The instruction decides which register is **selected**; only that one reacts.

blocks.title: Which edge?
blocks.md: In the reference design the capture and every shift happen on the **rising** edge of TCK, while the update latches load on the **falling** edge in Update-DR. The update therefore happens half a clock after the last shift — after the shift register has settled.

blocks.title: The same signals everywhere
blocks.md: Exactly these signals — select, capture, shift, update, reset, clock — reappear as the **wrapper serial control** of IEEE 1500 and as the **scan interface** of IEEE 1687 instruments.
